The '''Nogoyevian War of Independence''', also called the '''Zhensanovian-Nogoyevian War''', was a 1949-1956 conflict between the [[Union of Zhensanov]] and [[Kingdom of Nogoyev]]. It began when Nogoyevian nationalists declared sovereignty from the Union and called for restoration of the Tsarist system.

The war was one of the major postwar crises that followed the [[Avant Great War]]. Zhensanov had committed resources to the [[United Alignment of Nations]] war effort, leaving internal grievances in Nogoyev to deepen during the final years of the global war.

== Background ==

Nogoyev had been incorporated into the Union of Zhensanov in the mid-19th century. The source record says this incorporation was initially supported by many Nogoyevians because the six Zhensanovian constituent nations shared close cultural and historical ties.

Over time, centralization under the [[Zhensanov United Party]] created resentment. Nogoyev's agrarian economy lagged behind the Union's industrial centers, while local leaders accused the central government of taxing Nogoyevian agricultural produce and resources to fund development elsewhere.

The [[All-Nationalist Nogoyev Party]] turned those grievances into a sovereignty movement. It called for democratic reforms, local autonomy, and the restoration of the Tsar as a symbol of Nogoyevian continuity.

== Outbreak ==

In early 1949, after protests, strikes, clandestine organizing, and clashes with Union authorities, Nogoyevian leaders declared sovereignty from Zhensanov. The Union government rejected the declaration and ordered a military intervention.

Union forces crossed into Nogoyev in April 1949 expecting a rapid campaign. Instead they faced prepared regular units, local militias, guerrilla networks, fortified cities, and broad civilian support for the independence movement.

== Course Of The War ==

The early war centered on attempts to break Nogoyevian resistance through rapid invasion, bombing, and pressure against major cities. The [[Battle of Migov]] became a years-long urban battle and one of the bloodiest engagements of the conflict. The [[Siege of Boten]] showed that the Union could not easily seize major coastal and industrial centers despite naval superiority.

By 1952, Nogoyev had shifted from mostly guerrilla defense to organized counteroffensives. The [[Battle of the Black Hills]] and the winter offensive west of Migov pushed Union forces away from key urban areas. By late 1953, the [[Battle of Svoshchensk Forestry]] marked the effective end of the ground war inside Nogoyevian territory.

Air and naval campaigns continued to shape the conflict. Zhensanov had stronger fleet and air assets, but poor logistics, coastal defenses, and Nogoyevian anti-aircraft fire prevented decisive control.

== Ceasefire And Cold Peace ==

After 1954, the war became a fortified border conflict. Skirmishes, artillery exchanges, raids, and air incidents continued, but neither side could achieve a decisive breakthrough.

In early 1956, international pressure and war exhaustion produced a ceasefire. No comprehensive peace treaty resolved the underlying dispute. The result was the [[Zhensanov-Nogoyev cold peace]], with both states heavily armed along the border and politically unreconciled.

== Legacy ==

The war created the modern [[Tsardom of Nogoyev]] and permanently changed Zhensanov's postwar politics. For Nogoyev, it became the foundational independence struggle. For Zhensanov, it exposed the limits of central control after the Great War and remained a major source of security pressure by 1994.
